description: Three-panel composite figure that combines one process schematic with two specimen-geometry drawings; no micrographs or measured data curves are present. (a) is a schematic plot of Temperature (vertical axis, no numeric scale) versus Time (horizontal axis, no numeric scale) containing two thermal cycles. The first cycle rises across a blue dashed horizontal line labelled "Ac1" to a plateau marked "holding" (red arrow) with a 4 h isotherm, then a "forging" step (red arrow), then "air cooling" back to room temperature. The second cycle overlays four schedules labelled 950 °C and 850 °C (black curves) and 750 °C and 650 °C (red curves), each with a 2 h isotherm, a "rolling" step (red arrow) and "air cooling". (b) is the rod-shaped tensile specimen: circular-section gauge of 5 mm diameter (inset circle) and 25 mm gauge length, with a double-headed arrow marking RD along the axis. (c) is the Charpy V-notch bar: 55 mm along RD, 10 mm × 10 mm cross-section, ND labelled on the end face, and a V-notch machined into the top (rolled) surface. Together the panels define the heat-treatment/rolling route and the two mechanical-test specimen geometries used for the R650-R950 series.

subfigures.description: Temperature-versus-Time schematic with unnumbered axes. Two cycles: first heating to a 'holding' plateau with 4 h isotherm, then 'forging' (red arrow) and 'air cooling'; second cycle with four schedules labelled 950 °C, 850 °C (black) and 750 °C, 650 °C (red), each with a 2 h hold, a 'rolling' step (red arrow) and 'air cooling'. A blue dashed line labelled 'Ac1' runs across the panel.

Drawing of the rod-shaped tensile specimen: cylindrical grip ends with a reduced circular gauge section, gauge diameter 5 mm (circular inset) and gauge length 25 mm, double-headed RD arrow along the specimen axis.
Drawing of the Charpy V-notch bar: rectangular prism 55 mm long (RD direction) with a 10 mm × 10 mm cross-section, end face labelled ND, and a V-notch cut into the top surface.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots Temperature (y-axis, no numeric ticks) against Time (x-axis, no numeric ticks); it is a schematic of two heat-treatment cycles, not measured data.
A horizontal blue dashed line labelled 'Ac1' spans panel (a) and both thermal cycles rise through it during heating.
In panel (a) the first cycle shows 'holding' (red arrow) with a 4 h isotherm at the top plateau, followed by a 'forging' step (red arrow) and 'air cooling' down to room temperature.

In panel (a) the second cycle shows four temperature schedules labelled 950 °C and 850 °C (black curves) and 750 °C and 650 °C (red curves), each held for 2 h, followed by a 'rolling' step (red arrow) and 'air cooling'.
Panel (b) depicts a rod-shaped tensile specimen with a 25 mm gauge length and 5 mm gauge diameter, with the axis labelled RD.
Panel (c) depicts a Charpy specimen of 55 mm length and 10 mm × 10 mm cross-section with ND labelled on the end face and a V-notch cut into the top surface.
The caption states that (a) is a schematic of the conducted heat treatments for the tested steel, (b) the geometry of tensile specimens and (c) the Charpy impact specimens.
The citing text states the steel ingot was homogenized at 1200 °C for 4 h, hot forged to 40 mm thickness and air cooled; specimens were then heated to 650, 750, 850 and 950 °C and held 2 h.
The citing text states hot rolling was conducted with a 60 % reduction ratio, reducing plate thickness from 40 mm to 16 mm, and the four groups were named R650, R750, R850 and R950.
The citing text states tensile specimens were rod-shaped with 25 mm gauge length and 5 mm diameter sampled along the rolling direction, tested at a crosshead speed of 1.5 mm/min.
The citing text states the Charpy V-notch specimens were 10 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm, the notch was machined on the rolled surface and the impact direction was perpendicular to RD.
The citing text states the four rolling temperatures were chosen to cover carbide precipitation/dissolution (≤750 °C) and DRX/DIFT (≥850 °C) regimes.
